headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from shared file/context flows; no critical compliance issue is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, clipboard, screenshots, and app context, while Semantic Kernel can ingest application-defined files and MCP/tool outputs. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path if B passes untrusted content into A or vice versa. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_b forwards untrusted file or tool output into agent_a prompts
IF agent_a reads attacker-controlled file or clipboard content as instructions
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and provenance header to all cross-agent content
Disable clipboard bridging between the agents
Require a human review step before any prompt includes external file text
Use allowlisted file paths only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/content separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read files, and A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code while B handles application context and secrets for plugins. If they share a workspace or memory path, sensitive material can flow from A into B's broader API surface. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a workspace, memory store, or copied artifacts
IF sensitive uploaded files or screenshots are forwarded from agent_a into agent_b tool calls
mitigations: Keep separate workspaces and separate credentials
Turn off automatic file forwarding between agents
Redact screenshots and uploaded files before handoff
Use per-agent least-privilege API keys
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention checks on inter-agent messages

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A cannot write files or modify git state, but agent B can write files and use MCP against application-defined files and external tools. If both are pointed at the same mutable resource, B can overwrite or race with A's read-based workflow. The conflict is real in default orchestration patterns, though not proven to be unrestricted on the same directory.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory or shared plugin state
IF agent_b writes artifacts that agent_a later reads as authoritative
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Lock shared files before B writes
Make A read-only on shared artifacts
Serialize write operations through one coordinator
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency or file-locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce file-derived analysis and screenshots, and B is a multi-agent orchestrator that can act on application context and plugin outputs. If B treats A's output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream tool calls or generated actions. The profiles do not show a built-in verification gate, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without an explicit verification step
IF agent_b uses A-generated facts to drive plugin calls or agent actions
mitigations: Require citations for every claim passed from A to B
Insert a verification prompt before any action-taking tool call
Limit B to read-only summarization of A output
Log and diff A output before reuse
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A is vendor-mediated with OpenAI-managed services and touches uploaded files, screenshots, and voice; B is a library that can route data to Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Hugging Face, MCP servers, or OpenAPI tools. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch by themselves, so only a low compliance risk is evidenced, and B is cited because it can determine the downstream destination.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated data is routed from agent_a into a non-compliant agent_b deployment
IF retention or logging settings differ across the two agents for the same data class
mitigations: Confirm data residency for each API destination
Disable logging for regulated fields
Use a DPA-approved provider list
Separate regulated and unregulated workflows
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
